From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna@lumenix.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Lumenix renewal — usage & performance concordance

Hi Anna,

Ahead of Lumenix's July renewal I pulled a compact health summary and a few options that would preserve performance while lowering unit cost. Quick highlights from Q1–Q2: 

- Tokens: ~1.8B total (Q1 0.9B / Q2 0.9B) with a 12% month-over-month increase in May driven by inference-heavy features.
- Latency: median tokens/sec was stable, but we saw 95th percentile spikes during peak ETL windows (east-us) — attached "latency-index-augmented-report.pdf" has the traces.
- Model mix: ~70% smaller decoder models for embeddings + 30% larger gen models for user-facing features; cost skew is concentrated in the latter.

Suggested next steps (pick one):
1) Staged commit uplift (12 months) — +20% committed tokens, 15% discount on gen model calls, priority dedicated pool for peak hours.
2) Headroom + burst credits (6 months) — smaller uplift, ability to burst with predictable overage tiers.
3) Maintain run-rate and apply batching/quantization recommendations — lower ops lift but slower cost improvement.

I've attached the token spend CSV and an MAP draft. If you want, Sean (CS) and Monica (Solutions/Ops) can join — they have concrete options for smoothing the latency spikes without major infra changes. 30-min sync slots available Tue/Wed this week.

Attachments: Lumenix_token_spend_Q1-Q2-2028.csv; latency-index-augmented-report.pdf; mutual-action-plan-Lumenix-May-2028.xlsx

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Kim / Monica — quick operational notes to support the external ask: 

- Dedicated pool behavior: we can guarantee a latency SLO boundary for the 18:00–22:00 ET window by reserving an additional 2 RTX-class GPUs for the period, with autoscaling ramp during peak. That maps to the MAP's "peak-slab" pricing.
- Staged commit: propose 3-stage rollout (20% commit, review after 60 days, +10% optional uplift) to reduce procurement friction.
- Cost estimate: with the 20% commit uplift + scheduling the dedicated pool we expect a net monthly bill change of +$18k vs current run-rate but unit cost on gen calls drops ~14% — finance-friendly if product adoption continues.
- Overage policy: add a 30% burst credits buffer for the first 90 days to avoid surprise bills while patterns stabilize.

I'll prepare a short ops note to include in the MAP and the DocuSign addendum.

—Sean

Hi Anna / procurement team — following our internal ops alignment and your asks, here's a concise proposal for formal sign-off: 

Summary of recommendation
- Term: 12 months (Jul 1 2028 — Jun 30 2029)
- Commit uplift: +20% committed tokens over current run-rate
- Pricing: 15% gen-call discount off list for committed usage; embedding unit price reduced by 7%
- Operational guardrails: dedicated peak slab 18:00–22:00 ET; 90-day 30% burst credit buffer; staged review at 60 days.

Expected outcomes
- Unit cost for gen-heavy production calls drops ~14%
- 95th percentile latency improvement estimated at 18–25% during peak windows
- Predictable monthly billing with short-term headroom for adoption swings

Attachments: MAP workbook + ROI summary and token spend (same files as shared earlier).

Action items
1) Procurement: please validate DocuSign routing and confirm the signer (procurement@lumenix.ai or Jason). DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/Lumenix_Renewal_0828
2) Anna: confirm acceptance of the recommended path or propose the alternate (headroom + burst) by EOD Thu, Jun 28 so we can finalize SOW.
3) Internal: Sean/Monica to prepare the ops addendum and the 60-day review checklist.

If the plan looks good I'll circulate the DocuSign and schedule a 20-min kickoff for Jul 2 to enable the dedicated slab.

Thanks — appreciate the collaboration.

Best,
